10047397:
Testimony in Support of LD 1382 - An Act Regarding Dam Repair
D. Scott Miller, Blue Hill Select Board Member April 30, 2025
Members of the Criminal Justice and Public Safety Committee:
My name is Scott Miller, and I am a member of the Blue Hill Select Board. Blue Hill is one of four towns now evaluating the prospect of assuming ownership of a "high hazard" dam to protect our residents from the proposed abandonment of the dam by the current, commercial owner. I am testifying in favor of LD 1382.
Part of what makes Maine a special place are the ~6,000 lakes and ponds1 throughout the state. And many of these water bodies, including almost all of the best known and widely used ones, exist only because of dams constructed in the early 1900s or even the 1800s.
Many of these dams are now in the vicinity of their 100th birthdays and, while essential repair and maintenance work has occurred, we may be approaching an era where, for continued safety's sake, a more fundamental reconstruction of the dams will be necessary. Depending on the specific circumstances of an individual dam, this reconstruction--or even major repair work--can cost several million dollars. The largest dams are often hydroelectric power dams that are owned by businesses that have their own revenue stream to help pay for reconstruction. But many of the others do not.
The Committee and MEMA well understand the importance of timely maintenance and repair of the dams in our state--especially the ones designated as "high hazard" dams-- for public safety. A dam breach could cause catastrophic flooding of downstream properties far removed from the dam itself. So those downstream property owners rely on the dam owners to keep each dam in proper repair.
LD 1382 provides a mechanism to help finance the investment required to keep these dams safe--especially for dams that are not associated with commercial enterprises. The loan funds available through this legislation will help dam owners keep their dams in good repair and, thereby, enhance the safety and security of all Mainers in the vicinity of the dam.
I encourage the Committee to support this legislation.
1 Lakes Page - lake or pond, Bureau of Land and Water Quality, Maine DEP

Testimony in Support of LD1382 - An Act to Establish a Revolving Fund for Dam Maintenance
Dear Members of the Committee,
I am writing in strong support of LD1382, which would establish a revolving fund dedicated to the maintenance of Maine's dams. As someone who has spent a lifetime on the shores of Alamoosook Lake in Orland, I can attest to the critical importance of maintaining our dam--not only for ecological balance, but for the preservation of a unique way of life that has defined our town for generations.
For decades, families in Orland and beyond have gathered at this lake. Children learn to swim here, generations of Mainers have fished off its docks, and community members come together for events that strengthen the bonds of our small town. The dam helps ensure stable water levels that make all of this possible. Without it, the lake as we know it--and the role it plays in our lives--would be lost.
Beyond recreation and heritage, the lake supports vital ecological functions. It has become a nesting site for several species of waterfowl, including the iconic loon. Most critically, it plays an essential role in the life cycle of alewives, a migratory fish species that depends on consistent lake access for spawning. Removal or neglect of the dam would severely disrupt this delicate cycle and cause irreversible harm to native fish populations and the broader ecosystem.
Funding for dam maintenance is not just a matter of infrastructure--it is a matter of preserving Maine's natural, cultural, and community heritage. I urge you to support LD1382 so that communities like ours can continue to protect and enjoy these invaluable resources for generations to come.
Sincerely, Lisa Deweese President, Alamoosook Lake Association Orland, Maine

Testimony in Support of Establishing a Statewide Revolving Fund for Lake Dam Repairs LD1382 Presented to the [Criminal Justice and Public Safety] By Philip A. Roberts Date: April 30, 2025
Chair, and distinguished members of the committee:
My name is Philip A. Roberts, I am a resident of Surry, Maine. I want to voice my strong support for the establishment of a revolving fund dedicated to the repair and rehabilitation of lake dams across the State of Maine.
Dams play a critical role in preserving Maine's environmental heritage, public safety, and recreational economy. Many of our lakes--iconic to our state's natural identity--depend on dams for maintaining water levels that support ecosystems, fisheries, property values, and local tourism. However, many of these dams are aging, structurally compromised, and under increasing strain from extreme weather events brought on by climate change. Unfortunately, municipalities, lake associations, and private dam owners often lack the financial resources necessary to carry out the extensive repairs or upgrades needed to bring these structures into compliance with safety standards. Without timely intervention, dam failures could pose serious risks to downstream communities, wildlife habitats, and drinking water supplies. These risks come at far greater costs--both economic and environmental--than proactive maintenance. A state-administered revolving loan fund would provide a sustainable, long-term mechanism to support dam owners and stakeholders in making necessary repairs. By offering low- or no-interest loans with flexible repayment terms, the fund would incentivize early action, distribute the financial burden fairly, and preserve public and private infrastructure for generations to come. Moreover, this fund aligns with Maine's broader commitment to environmental stewardship and climate resilience. The proactive maintenance of our lake dams will ensure stable water levels, preserve biodiversity, and sustain the recreational opportunities that fuel our local economies and make Maine a destination for residents and visitors alike.
I respectfully urge the committee to advance this initiative and secure the resources necessary to protect our lakes, our communities, and our future.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely, Philip A. Roberts 8 Hewey Lane Surry, Maine 04684 Phil.roberts@verizon.net

Dear Members of the Maine State Legislature,

LD 1382: An Act Regarding Dam Repair

Sponsored by:

Representative Nina Milliken (Blue Hill)

Co-sponsored by: Representative Steven Bishop (Bucksport)

Senator Nicole Grohoski (Hancock)

Senator David Hagan (Penobscot)

Criminal Justice and Public Safety Committee

I support the above-mentioned piece of legislation. As a property owner on Toddy Pond, Penobscot Maine, I am very familiar with the challenges many communities and lake associations face in maintaining dams which in many cases are over 100 years old. Preservation of these dams and the bodies of water they impound helps to protect wildlife, recreation, safe drinking water for neighboring wells, water for fire suppression and area economic benefits. Recent studies have indicated Toddy Pond and adjacent Alamoosook Lake contribute over $100,000,000 in economic benefit that includes lost tax dollars for surrounding towns. This would all be lost if the dams were gone.
Despite these valuable benefits, the cost of maintaining, repairing and/or improving these impoundments is often beyond the reach of local municipalities, lake associations and lakefront owners. This legislation would facilitate the local ownership and maintenance of these structures so vital to our communities. Additionally, it would enhance public safety by facilitating repair and maintenance of "high risk" dams such as the ones on Toddy Pond and Alamoosook Lake.
By creating a fund which would provide loans to the communities and organizations owning and maintaining these dams, this legislation would provide all of the benefits listed above in a way which minimizes the cost to the States infrastructure costs.
For these reasons, I strongly support this legislation.
